scope: Only concrete omissions already named by the current hip-FAI and MRI-ankle walkthrough findings. Preserve all existing structures, parts, checklists, worksheets and required representations.

RA_HIP.supports: Local AIIS morphology and injury-related ossification can be alternative osseous pain generators; morphology alone is not a clinical impingement diagnosis.

AIIS_CT_2013.supports: AIIS caudal extent and the intervening ilium wall are evaluated relative to the acetabular rim. Source figure captions 2–5 separate smooth wall, prominence at the rim and distal extension.
AIIS_CT_2013.limits: Morphological groupings and simulated motion from selected symptomatic cohorts do not independently diagnose pain or validate an unrelated atlas mesh.

AIIS_AP_2017.supports: A conspicuous AIIS projection on AP imaging can prompt further assessment, but AP pelvis alone cannot reliably distinguish the full 3D morphological classes.
AIIS_AP_2017.access: Primary indexed abstract reviewed; full-text claims not imported.

RA_ANKLE.supports: Accessory muscle tissue may resemble usual muscle on MRI; local course and surrounding anatomy require inspection. Its examples include accessory soleus and accessory FHL/FDL.

PQ_MRI_2025.supports: 1160 ankle examinations assessed a lateral-compartment peroneus quartus separately from usual peroneal tendons and studied adjacent tendon disease. Figure 1 depicts one origin/insertion pattern, not a universal variant.
PQ_MRI_2025.access: Primary indexed abstract/figure caption reviewed; publisher fetch returned 429. No media acquired.

ASM_MRI_CADAVER_2011.supports: Accessory soleus attachment patterns differ between specimens; the MRI cases had a separate medial-calcaneal tendon, while dissections also showed other attachments.
ASM_MRI_CADAVER_2011.limits: Do not substitute ordinary soleus anatomy or impose one distal attachment on every accessory soleus.

FDAL_CADAVER_1997.supports: Two accessory flexor digitorum longus specimens were in the deep posterior compartment and differed in size/origin.

FDAL_MRI_SURGERY_2024.supports: Bilateral MRI and surgery in one patient document the accessory muscle and its relationship to tibial nerve and vessels in the tarsal tunnel; dynamic compression cannot be inferred from a neutral static reference.
FDAL_MRI_SURGERY_2024.media_rights: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 at publisher; factual reference only, no commercial media import or adaptation.

effective_walkthrough_evidence.label: Alternative pain generators
effective_walkthrough_evidence.detail: Assess periarticular tendons, bursae, muscles and the visible pelvic structures.
findings: Prominent anterior inferior iliac spine extending to the acetabular rim (subspine impingement morphology).
Gluteus [medius / minimus] tendinopathy [with partial tear] at the greater trochanter.
Femoral head subchondral fracture or osteonecrosis.

findings: Soft-tissue thickening in the anterolateral gutter, compatible with anterolateral impingement in the appropriate clinical setting.

Moderate tibiotalar effusion with synovial thickening.

append_structures.name: Peroneus quartus (fibularis quartus) muscle
append_structures.condition: For the explicitly named accessory-muscle finding when this variant is present/suspected on the examined side, within the actual MRI coverage. Record absent, not seen or outside coverage distinctly; do not assert a variant exists in every examination. Belly/course and each attachment retain their acquisition limits. Map its captured course in the lateral/retromalleolar region separately from fibularis brevis and longus; do not relabel fibularis tertius as this variant. Individual anatomy and pathology need independent source/examination review; static geometry does not establish symptom causation or dynamic compression.

msk_atlas_hip.limits: Whole right hip bone is not independent proof of AIIS caudal extent or the subspine region. Rectus femoris tendon material is not a measured direct-head footprint.

bodyparts3d_hip.limits: Whole bone and broad family selection do not bind or validate AIIS substructures.

msk_atlas_ankle.limits: Fibularis tertius, longus, brevis and FDL are ordinary named source objects, not any of the three proposed accessory variants.

malaya_mri_ankle.limits: Usual soleus, FDL and fibularis longus source muscle units do not prove accessory soleus, FDAL or PQ.

rectus_course_image.limits: Existing local direct/indirect tendon course panels do not establish AIIS/subspine morphology or complete direct-head origin.
